description:
FILED s473h (Opus, 2026-09-08) as the owner of ir-conform case 253-string,
taken over from #1249(5), which asked only for `exists $string->{k}` to die.
MEASURED first: `exists` is not a singleton â the WHOLE arrow-deref family
diverges the same way, and the cause is the one already ruled in
`docs/not-supported.md` Â§"`use strict 'refs'` is not enforced â every
dereference is the `no strict` one".

THE MEASUREMENT (scratch/s473h/probe/m5.pl, `use strict` at the top;
perl 5.40.3 vs PCL at a9f2a264; `$ns = "plain"`, `$u` undef, `$n = 5`):

  spelling            perl                                    PCL
  $ns->{k}            dies Can't use string ("plain") as a    [undef]
                        HASH ref while "strict refs" in use
  exists $ns->{k}     dies (same)                             []
  delete $ns->{k}     dies (same)                             [u]
  keys %$ns           dies (same)                             [0]
  $ns->[0]            dies â¦as an ARRAY refâ¦                  [undef]
  exists $ns->[0]     dies â¦as an ARRAY refâ¦                  []
  delete $ns->[0]     dies â¦as an ARRAY refâ¦                  [u]
  $ns->{k} = 1        dies â¦as a HASH refâ¦                    ok
  $n->{k}   ($n = 5)  dies Can't use string ("5") â¦           SBCL type error
  $u->{k}   (undef)   [undef]                                 [undef]   AGREE
  exists $u->{k}      []                                      []        AGREE

So a fix for `exists` alone would be one arm of a nine-arm family, and it
would have to invent the strict state that the other eight arms need anyway.

WHY IT IS NOT A SINGLETON FIX.  `use strict 'refs'` is a LEXICAL COMPILE-TIME
HINT.  PCL tracks no strict state at all (the same gap as `$^H`/`%^H`), and
every site that resolves a string in reference position â p-ensure-hashref,
p-ensure-arrayref, p-cast-%, p-cast-@, p-cast-$ â goes to the package
variable unconditionally.  Lifting it takes the model
`docs/not-supported.md` names: one compiled-per-lexical-scope boolean the
reference resolvers consult (a SITE argument, not a dynamic variable â strict
is lexical, so a dynamic binding would leak into called subs), plus perl's two
message texts.  Same shape as #221's warnings model.

ONE RESIDUE THAT IS *NOT* THE PRAGMA, and is a real rule-12 bug: with a
NUMERIC "reference" (`my $n = 5; $n->{k}`) PCL does not take the symbolic path
at all â it reaches SBCL's GETHASH and dies

    Value of pcl::h in (sb-impl::gethash3 k h nil) is 5, not a hash-table.

which is a host-level failure, not catchable in Perl terms.  perl dies
`Can't use string ("5") as a HASH ref while "strict refs" in use` under
strict, and treats it as the symbolic name `$main::{5}` without.  p-cast-$
documents the same NUMBER/string ambiguity for the scalar spelling (#505 /
#551): a number falls through deliberately there.  The hash/array spellings
should at least reach `%p-not-a-ref`-style perl-shaped diagnostics rather than
an SBCL type error.  Small, independent of the pragma; worth taking as a
filler.

CORPUS: ir-conform/known-fail.tsv row `253-string` re-pointed from 1249 to
this task.  Its residue is TWO causes: this one (four `exists â¦` lines are
printed where perl has already died) and #1247 (exit 255 vs 0), so it stays
known-fail even after the pragma lands until #1247 does too.


=== s497b (2026-09-26): enforced by #2103 except the write ===
The nine-spelling table re-measured under `use strict` (scratch/s497b/p1390.pl): $ns->{k}, exists/delete $ns->{k}, keys %$ns, $ns->[0], exists/delete $ns->[0], $n->{k} all DIE as in perl now; `$ns->{k} = 1` (the WRITE) still lives -> #2403.  ir-conform 253-string: see the ir-conform run of s497b.
subject: `use strict 'refs'` is not enforced: `$string->{k}` / `exists` / `delete` / `keys %$s` answer the no-strict symbolic ref where perl dies -- needs the strict-hints model; owner of ir-conform 253-string, taken over from #1249(5)
